newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - OCT 24.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - OCT 24.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- The Parliament's Economic Committee backed the appointment of Judit Csiha as privatisation minister, without vote against.

- The parliamentary committee set up to inverstigate the privatisation scandal said there was hope that an advisor would return the whole irregular payment of 800 million forint which she had received from the privatisation agency.

- The police initiated proceedings against three participants of the Hungarian Welfare Alliance's rally on Wednesday, for allegedly hurting public health rules and abusing the right of public meetings.
- The Hungarian Television will not broadcast the Newcastle-Ferencvaros soccer UEFA Cup second tie because a commercial channel bought the broadcasting right.

- The government will discuss again on Thursday the Government Supervisory Office's report on the debt and bank consolidation programme , which was worth 350 billion forints, and will decide on what steps are necessary.
